name: MedXpertQA
intro: MedXpertQA是一个专家级医学多项选择基准。论文从37,543道美国执照考试、17类专科委员会考试及影像丰富来源题目出发，经人类难度、AI专家、编辑距离与MedCPT语义相似度筛选，再以GPT-4o/Claude改写扩充并由持证医师逐题复核，最终保留4,460题：Text 2,455题、MM 2,005题，各含5题开发集。测试集共4,450题，覆盖17个专业、11个身体系统以及Reasoning/Understanding两类能力。
org: Tsinghua University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
build_method: 考试题筛选, LLM增强, 持证医师审核
modality: 文本, 图像, 多模态
eval_feature: 领域特定, 多模态, 推理导向
build_method_en: Exam Filtering, LLM Augmentation, Licensed-physician Review
intro_en: MedXpertQA is an expert-level medical multiple-choice benchmark. The paper starts from 37,543 questions drawn from U.S. licensing exams, 17 specialty-board families, and image-rich sources; applies human-difficulty, AI-expert, edit-distance, and MedCPT semantic-similarity filters; rewrites and expands items with GPT-4o and Claude; and has licensed physicians review every item. The final 4,460 questions comprise 2,455 Text and 2,005 MM items, each with a five-example development set. Its 4,450 test questions span 17 specialties, 11 body systems, and Reasoning/Understanding categories.

drawio_review_note: Paper/source audit: arXiv:2501.18362v3, Sections 3.1-4.3 and Appendices C, E, G-I, cross-checked against TsinghuaC3I/MedXpertQA commit 47b29e17b8d980e03b62a22927cff775016c6afd and ungated Hugging Face revision 7e7c465a68eb2b866926bfa59c8c9d17a8daba65. The count-bearing construction path follows Table 1 and the introduction: collect 37,543 questions (26,675 Text and 10,868 MM) from USMLE, COMLEX, 17 American specialty-board families, ACR DXIT/TXIT, EDiR, NEJM Image Challenge, and other authoritative exam/textbook sources, together with human response distributions, explanations, and prior difficulty labels. Human filtering uses a Brier score over answer-choice distributions, three normalized prior-difficulty levels, adaptive thresholds spanning the 3rd to 25th score percentiles, and leaves the 16.78% without required annotations unfiltered, yielding 10,146. AI filtering then yields 4,737 using an eight-model basic/advanced pool, four attempts per basic expert, and fourteen sampling votes per question; the paper states that any basic expert scoring 4/4 makes an item too easy and that all-experts-wrong items are retained, but does not fully specify the intermediate-case rule. Section 3.2 labels AI as Step 1 and Human as Step 2, contradicting the introduction and Table 1 count order; the diagram uses the only sequential order that reconciles 37,543 → 10,146 → 4,737 and records this discrepancy rather than hiding it. Edit-distance filtering retains 4,713, then MedCPT-Query-Encoder cosine similarity with IQR outlier detection retains 4,683, removing the easier member of a near-duplicate pair. GPT-4o-2024-11-20 and Claude-3.5-Sonnet-20241022 rewrite questions and generate distractors; low-response distractors are removed while preserving the gold choice and at least two distractors, then Text is expanded to ten options and MM fixed at five. Licensed physicians correct most question/option errors and delete 223 items, producing 2,455 Text plus 2,005 MM questions. The pinned public release proves five development examples per subset and 2,450 Text plus 2,000 MM test items; it contains 2,852 test images and six development images. The paper itself conflicts: Section 3.1 says 2,839 images across 2,005 MM questions, while Table 2 says 2,852 across the 2,000-question MM test set; the public test matches Table 2. GPT-4o labels Diagnosis/Treatment/Basic-Medicine tasks and Reasoning/Understanding types. The paper calls its type-label audit a random 10% but reports 490 Text plus 400 MM items, which is 20% of the 4,450 test set; 39/890 were mislabeled, approximately 4.3%. Evaluation is multiple-choice only, not open-ended or conversational: the standard path uses a medical-assistant system role, zero-shot CoT, a second answer-trigger turn, and greedy decoding where available. Standard outputs first try an exact split on the answer-trigger phrase; if absent, the pinned utility next tries the substring ' answer is ', and if that also fails it scans the whole second-turn reply. It then regex-matches A-J for Text or A-E for MM and uses the first match; empty extraction is wrong. The official eval notebook deliberately reparses the two incompatible cases rather than sending them through that utility: QVQ output is split case-insensitively on 'final answer' and uses the first following letter when the phrase exists or the last letter otherwise, while DeepSeek-R1 requires and extracts a boxed A-J/A-E choice. The scorer checks exact label equality; the notebook asserts source/output length and ID alignment, so each reported denominator is all outputs retained for the relevant Text/MM and Reasoning/Understanding slice. Cost-limited o1 and o3-mini runs sample 10% from each type in each subset with seed 42. The paper evaluates 18 models, whereas the current README says 17. Public data, images, evaluator, MIT license, and leaderboard exist, but the official repository does not release the filtering, rewriting, augmentation, or expert-review construction implementation; the diagram marks that reproducibility boundary. Formal publication evidence [site-a11u-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2013×1021 (English) and 2013×1021 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2011×1019 and 2011×1019. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
